pharm-micro:bactmap.q: Which class inhibits the 30S ribosomal subunit?

A 21-year-old student has 2 weeks of low-grade fever, dry cough and malaise; chest X-ray shows patchy interstitial infiltrates and cold agglutinin titers are elevated. The causative organism has no cell wall. Which antibiotic class would be ineffective?
pharm-micro:bactmap.e: Mycoplasma pneumoniae lacks peptidoglycan, so cell-wall inhibitors have no target. Ribosomal (macrolide, tetracycline) and gyrase inhibitors remain active.

pharm-micro:penicillin.q: Penicillinase-resistant penicillins (nafcillin, dicloxacillin) are used for:

A 24-year-old man has a painless, indurated genital ulcer with a clean base and nontender inguinal lymphadenopathy for 1 week. Dark-field microscopy of the ulcer exudate shows motile spirochetes. Most appropriate treatment?
o: Benzathine penicillin G, single IM dose
pharm-micro:penicillin.e: Primary syphilis (Treponema pallidum) is treated with IM benzathine penicillin G. Acyclovir treats HSV, whose ulcers are painful and vesicular.

pharm-micro:ceph.q: Aztreonam is safe in penicillin allergy because:
o: It is a carbapenem, not a penicillin
It is given orally, avoiding sensitization
It is a monobactam with no cross-reactivity
It lacks a β-lactam ring and cannot bind PBPs

pharm-micro:ceph.q: A 62-year-old man on mechanical ventilation in the ICU develops fever and purulent sputum. Sputum culture grows an oxidase-positive, lactose-nonfermenting gram-negative rod with a grape-like odor. Which cephalosporin would cover this organism?
pharm-micro:ceph.e: Pseudomonas aeruginosa is covered by the 4th-generation cefepime (and ceftazidime). Ceftriaxone lacks reliable antipseudomonal activity.

pharm-micro:vanco.q: Daptomycin should not be used for:
pharm-micro:vanco.e: Inactivated by pulmonary surfactant. Monitor CK for myopathy.

pharm-micro:vanco.q: A 66-year-old man on hemodialysis has fever; blood cultures grow catalase-negative gram-positive cocci that grow in 6.5% NaCl and hydrolyze bile esculin. The isolate is resistant to vancomycin. Mechanism of resistance?
o: Altered PBP2a with low β-lactam affinity
Efflux pump that exports the drug
pharm-micro:vanco.e: VRE (Enterococcus) replaces the terminal D-Ala-D-Ala with D-Ala-D-Lac, which vancomycin binds poorly. PBP2a (mecA) is the mechanism of MRSA.

pharm-micro:aminogly.q: Aminoglycosides are ineffective against anaerobes because:

A 68-year-old man receiving IV ampicillin plus gentamicin for enterococcal endocarditis develops tinnitus and an unsteady gait, and his creatinine rises from 1.0 to 2.1 mg/dL. The drug responsible for these effects acts by:
o: Inhibiting DNA gyrase and topoisomerase IV
Binding the 30S subunit, causing mRNA misreading
pharm-micro:aminogly.e: Gentamicin (aminoglycoside) causes ototoxicity and nephrotoxicity; it binds the 30S subunit and blocks initiation/causes misreading. Ampicillin inhibits transpeptidation and lacks these toxicities.

pharm-micro:tetra.q: Tetracyclines should not be taken with:
pharm-micro:tetra.e: Divalent/trivalent cations chelate the drug → ↓ absorption.

pharm-micro:tetra.q: Tetracyclines are avoided in children because of:
o: Kernicterus from bilirubin displacement off albumin
Tooth discoloration and impaired bone growth
Gray baby syndrome and circulatory collapse

pharm-micro:tetra.q: A 30-year-old man from Connecticut has an expanding erythematous annular rash with central clearing on his thigh 10 days after a hiking trip, with fever and myalgia. The drug of choice acts by:
o: Blocking aminoacyl-tRNA binding at the 30S A site
pharm-micro:tetra.e: Early Lyme disease (erythema migrans) is treated with doxycycline, a tetracycline that blocks tRNA attachment at the 30S A site. Macrolides block 50S translocation.

o: Red man syndrome with rapid infusion
Achilles tendon rupture in the elderly

pharm-micro:macro.e: Good anaerobic coverage above the diaphragm.

pharm-micro:macro.q: A 4-year-old unvaccinated girl has 2 weeks of paroxysmal coughing spells ending in an inspiratory whoop and post-tussive vomiting. WBC is 32,000/mm³ with 75% lymphocytes. The drug of choice acts by:
pharm-micro:macro.e: Pertussis is treated with azithromycin, a macrolide that binds 23S rRNA of the 50S subunit and blocks translocation. Tetracyclines act at the 30S A site.

pharm-micro:linezolid.q: A 58-year-old woman taking sertraline is started on an oral antibiotic for vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus faecium bacteremia. Two days later she has agitation, hyperthermia, diaphoresis and inducible clonus. How does the new antibiotic kill bacteria?
o: Blocks aminoacyl-tRNA entry at the 30S site
Blocks formation of the 50S initiation complex
pharm-micro:linezolid.e: Linezolid (oral, VRE-active) is a weak MAO inhibitor that precipitates serotonin syndrome with SSRIs; it binds 23S rRNA and blocks the initiation complex. Daptomycin depolarizes membranes but is IV-only and not serotonergic.

o: Red man syndrome and tendon rupture
Tooth staining and gray baby syndrome
pharm-micro:folate.e: Also SJS, and kernicterus in neonates.

pharm-micro:folate.q: A 35-year-old man with HIV (CD4 120/mm³) takes TMP-SMX for Pneumocystis prophylaxis. Routine labs show K⁺ 6.1 mEq/L with normal renal function and no hemolysis. Mechanism of the hyperkalemia?
o: Trimethoprim blocks ENaC in the collecting duct
pharm-micro:folate.e: Trimethoprim acts like amiloride, blocking the collecting-duct epithelial Na⁺ channel and reducing K⁺ secretion. It does not inhibit aldosterone synthesis.

o: Red man syndrome on rapid infusion

pharm-micro:fq.q: A 72-year-old woman taking long-term prednisone for COPD is treated with levofloxacin for pneumonia. Five days later she feels a sudden pop in her posterior heel and cannot rise on her toes; squeezing the calf produces no plantar flexion. The antibiotic acts by:
o: Inhibiting DNA gyrase and topoisomerase IV
pharm-micro:fq.e: Fluoroquinolones cause tendinopathy/Achilles rupture (higher risk with age and corticosteroids) and inhibit DNA gyrase and topoisomerase IV. Rifampin inhibits RNA polymerase.

o: Red-orange body fluids and CYP induction
pharm-micro:tb.e: Give pyridoxine (B6). Ethambutol: optic neuritis; rifampin: orange fluids; pyrazinamide: hyperuricemia.

pharm-micro:tb.q: A 40-year-old man with cavitary pulmonary tuberculosis on four-drug therapy reports blurred vision; testing shows reduced acuity and red-green color blindness. The responsible drug acts by:
pharm-micro:tb.e: Ethambutol causes optic neuritis and blocks arabinosyltransferase (arabinogalactan synthesis). Isoniazid inhibits mycolic acid synthesis and causes peripheral neuropathy.

pharm-micro:prophylaxis.q: Pneumocystis prophylaxis in HIV begins at CD4 <:
Prophylaxis for MAC in HIV (when not on ART) at CD4 < 50:
pharm-micro:prophylaxis.e: Not needed if ART started promptly.

pharm-micro:prophylaxis.q: A 32-year-old man is newly diagnosed with HIV. CD4 count is 80/mm³ and Toxoplasma IgG is positive. Which single drug provides the most appropriate primary prophylaxis?
pharm-micro:prophylaxis.e: TMP-SMX covers both Pneumocystis (CD4 < 200) and Toxoplasma (CD4 < 100, IgG+). Dapsone alone covers Pneumocystis but not Toxoplasma.

o: β-glucan synthase in the cell wall

pharm-micro:fungmap.e: Used for invasive Candida and Aspergillus.

pharm-micro:fungmap.q: A 65-year-old man with acute myeloid leukemia and prolonged neutropenia develops fever and hemoptysis; CT shows a nodule with a surrounding halo. Biopsy shows septate hyphae branching at acute angles. The drug of choice acts by:
o: Binding ergosterol to form membrane pores
pharm-micro:fungmap.e: Invasive aspergillosis is treated with voriconazole, an azole that blocks ergosterol synthesis at 14α-demethylase. Amphotericin B binds ergosterol and is a second-line alternative.

pharm-micro:antiparasite.q: A 7-year-old girl has perianal itching that is worst at night. A cellophane tape test shows ova that are flattened on one side. She is treated with albendazole, which acts by:
pharm-micro:antiparasite.e: Enterobius vermicularis is treated with albendazole (or pyrantel); benzimidazoles bind β-tubulin. Increased Ca²⁺ permeability is praziquantel's mechanism.

o: Heme polymerase in the food vacuole

pharm-micro:malaria.q: Severe falciparum malaria is treated with:

A 28-year-old man returns from India with fevers recurring every 48 hours. Blood smear shows enlarged red cells with Schüffner dots. He is treated with chloroquine. Before adding a drug to prevent relapse, which test is required?
pharm-micro:malaria.e: P. vivax forms liver hypnozoites, eradicated by primaquine (or tafenoquine), which causes hemolysis in G6PD deficiency. HLA-B*57:01 is screened before abacavir.

pharm-micro:virmap.q: Acyclovir must be phosphorylated first by:

A 38-year-old man with AIDS (CD4 30/mm³) has blurred vision; fundoscopy shows fluffy yellow-white retinal lesions with hemorrhages. He is started on IV ganciclovir. Activation of this drug first requires:
o: No activation; binds the pyrophosphate site
pharm-micro:virmap.e: CMV retinitis: ganciclovir is monophosphorylated by the CMV UL97 kinase. Foscarnet needs no activation; HSV/VZV thymidine kinase activates acyclovir.

pharm-micro:hiv.q: A 34-year-old man is started on tenofovir, emtricitabine and efavirenz. Two weeks later he reports vivid dreams, insomnia and dizziness. The responsible drug acts by:
o: Blocking strand transfer by viral integrase
Competing with nucleotides at the RT active site
Binding reverse transcriptase at an allosteric site
Inhibiting cleavage of the gag-pol polyprotein
pharm-micro:hiv.e: Efavirenz (an NNRTI) causes CNS effects and binds RT away from the active site. Tenofovir and emtricitabine are NRTIs that compete at the active site.

pharm-micro:hep.q: A 40-year-old man has been HBsAg-positive for over 6 months. He is HBeAg-positive, HBV DNA is 2 × 10⁷ IU/mL and ALT is 3 times the upper limit of normal. He is started on tenofovir, which acts by:
o: Inhibiting the viral NS3/4A serine protease
Inhibiting the viral NS5B RNA polymerase
Blocking viral entry via the NTCP receptor
pharm-micro:hep.e: Chronic active hepatitis B is treated with tenofovir or entecavir, which inhibit the HBV polymerase's reverse transcriptase activity. NS5B and NS3/4A are hepatitis C targets.

title.th: เคสใหญ่: ไข้ คอแข็ง
title.en: Boss case: Fever and a stiff neck

boss.case: A 20-year-old university student has 12 hours of fever, severe headache, neck stiffness and a petechial rash on the legs. CSF: neutrophils, low glucose, high protein; Gram stain shows gram-negative diplococci.

qs.q: Empiric therapy for bacterial meningitis in a young adult:
qs.e: ± dexamethasone. Add ampicillin for Listeria if > 50 years or immunocompromised.

o: Inhibiting DNA gyrase and topo IV

qs.q: Close contacts should receive prophylaxis with:
qs.e: Single-dose ciprofloxacin or IM ceftriaxone is also used.

qs.q: Vancomycin is added mainly to cover:
qs.e: Penicillin/cephalosporin-resistant pneumococci; altered PBPs confer resistance.

qs.q: A vancomycin infusion reaction (diffuse flushing) is prevented by:
qs.e: Non-IgE histamine release, not an allergy.

title.th: เพิ่งพบติดเชื้อ HIV

stem.th: ชาย 29 ปี ตรวจพบ HIV จากการตรวจคัดกรอง CD4 180 cells/mm³ viral load สูง
stem.en: A 29-year-old man is diagnosed with HIV on screening; CD4 180 cells/mm³, high viral load.

steps.q: Prophylaxis needed at this CD4 count:

info.th: ถ้าจะใช้ abacavir

steps.e: Tenofovir alafenamide has less renal/bone toxicity.
